   178	                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
   179	                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)
   182	
   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers ==================================…1646 tokens truncated…se no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/call.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    75	
    76	  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
    78	  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
    79	  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
    80	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    81	        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    82	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    83	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
    84	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    85	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    86	
    87	  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
    88	  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
    90	       <env> L:Int </env>
    91	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
    93	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
    94	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
    95	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/operators.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/int.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/int.k — MPY-INT
     2	// Int cases of the operator dispatch; Python // and % are floored (pyMod).
     3	
     4	module MPY-INT
     5	  imports MPY-CORE
     6	
     7	  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I
     8	
     9	  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    12	  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
    13	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
    14	  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
    15	  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
    16	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    17	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    18	
    19	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    20	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2
    21	
    22	  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
    23	  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
    24	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    25	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    26	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    27	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2
    28	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/controls.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/controls.k — MPY-CONTROLS
     2	
     3	module MPY-CONTROLS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-TUPLE
     6	  imports MPY-ITER
     7	
     8	  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
     9	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    10	       <env> L:Int </env>
    11	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    12	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    13	       <env> L:Int </env>
    14	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    15	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    16	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    17	        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
    18	       [priority(40)]
    19	
    20	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    21	       <env> L:Int </env>
    22	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
    23	       requires X in_keys(M)
    24	  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
    27	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
    28	       <env> L:Int </env>
    29	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    30	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/bool.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/bool.k — MPY-BOOL
     2	// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are
     3	// value-returning short-circuit over any Vals, per Python).
     4	
     5	module MPY-BOOL
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	
     8	  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)
     9	
    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    14	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    15	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    16	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    17	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    18	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    19	       requires truthy(V)
    20	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    21	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    22	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>

     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

    16	  rule <k> #applyK(toTuple, ACC:Vals) => tuple(vals2valSeq(ACC)) ... </k>

    18	  rule applyCmp("==", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    19	  // membership routes through the same k-cell fold as lists (list.k)
    20	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ... </k>
    21	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    22	  // t.index(v): first index of v (ValueError out of subset)

    24	  syntax Int ::= idxOfVS(ValSeq, Val, Int) [function]

    26	  rule idxOfVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val, I:Int) => idxOfVS(R, V, I +Int 1)

    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)

    30	  // ==== target binding: bind a Name or a TupleExpr target to a value ========

    34	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    35	  rule <k> #bindTgt(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    36	       <env> L:Int </env>
    37	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>

    39	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))

    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), tuple(VS:ValSeq)) => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    43	  rule <k> #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), list(VS:ValSeq))  => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    44	  rule <k> #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), ref(H:Int)) => #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS), V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	
    48	  // ==== unpacking: a, b = <tuple|list> (RHS evaluated by strictness) ========
    49	  syntax KItem ::= #unpackSeq(Exprs, ValSeq)
    50	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), tuple(VS:ValSeq)) => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), list(VS:ValSeq))  => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), ref(H:Int)) => Assign(TupleExpr(TS), V) ... </k>
    53	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    54	       [priority(40)]

     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule

     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)

    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34

    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37

    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read and summarize every required legacy-selected-stage1 record."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path("/generation-evidence")
TRACE = next((ROOT / "codex-trace").rglob("*.jsonl"))
RECORDS = [
    Path("/run.json"),
    Path("/task.json"),
    Path("/generation-result.json"),
    ROOT / "invocation.json",
    ROOT / "metrics.json",
    ROOT / "usage.json",
]
TEXT = [
    ROOT / "codex-last.txt",
    ROOT / "codex-output.log",
    ROOT / "prompt.txt",
]


def digest(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def main() -> None:
    for path in RECORDS:
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        parsed = json.loads(raw)
        print(
            f"JSON {path} bytes={len(raw)} sha256={digest(raw)} "
            f"top_keys={sorted(parsed)}"
        )

    for path in TEXT:
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
        print(
            f"TEXT {path} bytes={len(raw)} lines={len(text.splitlines())} "
            f"sha256={digest(raw)} nul_bytes={raw.count(bytes([0]))}"
        )

    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    tool_inputs: list[str] = []
    line_count = 0
    for line_count, line in enumerate(TRACE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        item = json.loads(line)
        payload = item.get("payload", {})
        key = f"{item.get('type')}/{payload.get('type')}"
        counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        if payload.get("type") == "function_call":
            tool_inputs.append(payload.get("arguments", ""))
        if payload.get("type") == "custom_tool_call":
            tool_inputs.append(payload.get("input", ""))
    print(
        f"TRACE {TRACE} lines={line_count} bytes={TRACE.stat().st_size} "
        f"sha256={digest(TRACE.read_bytes())}"
    )
    for key, count in sorted(counts.items()):
        print(f"TRACE_EVENT {key} {count}")

    joined = "\n".join(tool_inputs)
    print(f"TOOL_INPUT_COUNT {len(tool_inputs)}")
    print(
        "REFERENCE_SEMANTICS_PATCH_MENTIONS "
        f"{joined.count('*** Update File: /work/reference-semantics') + joined.count('*** Add File: /work/reference-semantics')}"
    )
    print(f"KPROVE_COMMAND_MENTIONS {joined.count('kprove ')}")
    print(f"KOMPILE_COMMAND_MENTIONS {joined.count('kompile ')}")
    print(f"APPLY_PATCH_MENTIONS {joined.count('*** Begin Patch')}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

+# Independent adversarial review: 49-modp
+
+This audit reconstructed the candidate from source under the supplied semantics.
+The positive K claim is sound and non-vacuous on its stated domain, but it
+materially narrows the HumanEval source-contract domain without a source
+precondition authorizing that restriction. Under the benchmark-specific
+decision rule, that is not a legitimate proof of the full task.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares:
+
+- problem `49-modp`, condition `semantics`;
+- `record_layout = legacy-selected-stage1`;
+- `semantics_mode = SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`; and
+- complete input provenance with the launcher paths supplied through
+  `container_paths`.
+
+The launcher and provenance gate passed:
+
+- `/audit-campaign-lock.json` is JSON-equal to the `audit_campaign` block and
+  has the recorded SHA-256
+  `ad5dfcc006af70c4d0d2c6641f0878a6c54a266e9ad2b54cd225b2381a78d745`.
+- The required layout records are readable regular files:
+  `/run.json`, `/task.json`, `/generation-result.json`,
+  `/generation-evidence/invocation.json`, `metrics.json`,
+  `codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`, `prompt.txt`, and the structured trace.
+  `usage.json` is present and was inspected. Historical
+  `runtime-metrics.json` is absent, which is permitted for this layout.
+- The full generation output (14,319 lines) and all 181 JSONL trace records
+  were read. The trace contains 38 tool inputs, 13 `kprove` command mentions,
+  seven `kompile` command mentions, and no patch targeting
+  `reference-semantics/`.
+- Every launcher-recorded scalar file hash checked by the reviewer matches.
+- Candidate `prompt.py` and `py2mpy.py` are byte-identical to the trusted
+  mounts.
+- The candidate and trusted supplied-semantics trees have exactly the same 24
+  files, path types, and bytes. Neither tree contains a symlink. The required
+  trusted semantics mount is present, consistent with `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`.
+- All five required proof artifacts are nonempty regular files. Candidate
+  caches were not copied or reused.
+
+Evidence:
+[integrity log](/audit-output/evidence/01-integrity.log),
+[record scan](/audit-output/evidence/01-generation-record-scan.log), and
+[trace action extraction](/audit-output/evidence/01-generation-trace-actions.log).
+The reviewer scripts are
+[integrity_check.py](/audit-output/evidence/integrity_check.py) and
+[generation_record_scan.py](/audit-output/evidence/generation_record_scan.py).
+
+There is no audit-infrastructure breach.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Source contract and implementations
+
+The trusted prompt declares `modp(n: int, p: int)` and says: “Return 2^n
+modulo p (be aware of numerics).” It gives five positive-modulus,
+nonnegative-exponent examples, but states no input precondition.
+
+The trusted canonical implementation initializes `ret = 1`, loops over
+`range(n)`, updates `ret = (2 * ret) % p`, and returns `ret`.
+
+The submitted program is:
+
+```python
+def modp(n: int, p: int):
+    """Return 2^n modulo p."""
+    return (2 ** n) % p
+```
+
+Running the trusted translator in scratch regenerated `solution.mpy` with byte
+identity (exit 0):
+[regeneration log](/audit-output/evidence/02-regeneration.log) and
+[regenerated term](/audit-output/evidence/regenerated-solution.mpy).
+
+### Independent differential test
+
+The reviewer-authored
+[differential_test.py](/audit-output/evidence/differential_test.py) imports the
+trusted canonical and generated entries under distinct module names. It
+exercised:
+
+- all five documented examples;
+- `n = 0` (the canonical loop's empty boundary), `n = 1`, and nearby values;
+- `p = 1`, `p = 2`, and nearby values;
+- exponent boundaries 63/64/65, a large `(4096, 65537)` case;
+- a complete grid `0 <= n <= 32`, `1 <= p <= 64`; and
+- 500 deterministic generated pairs with `0 <= n <= 5000`,
+  `1 <= p <= 10000`.
+
+There were 2,619 unique cases. The generated program agreed with the prompt's
+`pow(2, n, p)` value on all of them. It differed from the canonical once:
+
+```text
+n=0, p=1: canonical=1, generated=0, pow(2,0,1)=0
+```
+
+Thus the generated program is mathematically faithful to the prose at that
+boundary, while the canonical loop has an empty-loop boundary defect. The
+command intentionally exits 1 so this disagreement cannot be overlooked:
+[differential log](/audit-output/evidence/02-differential.log).
+
+The more serious adequacy issue is domain scope. The prompt's annotated source
+domain is two integers and contains no `n >= 0` or `p > 0` precondition. Even
+if modulus zero is excluded as undefined, the canonical terminates on negative
+`n` and on negative nonzero `p`. Diagnostics show material differences:
+
+```text
+(-1, 3): canonical 1, generated 0.5
+(0, -5): canonical 1, generated -4
+```
+
+The candidate theorem excludes all such inputs. The examples do not create a
+source-level restriction, and finitely observed test ranges cannot do so.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+Only source artifacts were copied to `/tmp/audit-work/49-modp`; the trusted
+reference-semantics tree was used, and no candidate-built definition or cache
+was reused. Tool versions were independently checked as K v7.1.293:
+[toolchain log](/audit-output/evidence/03-toolchain.log).
+
+Fresh builds:
+
+```text
+kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition runtime-kompiled -w none
+```
+
+Exit 0:
+[LLVM build log](/audit-output/evidence/03-kompile-llvm.log).
+
+```text
+kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
+  --main-module MODP-VERIFICATION --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition verification-kompiled -w none
+```
+
+Exit 0:
+[Haskell build log](/audit-output/evidence/03-kompile-haskell.log).
+
+The candidate has exactly one positive target claim. Its independent command
+was:
+
+```text
+kprove spec.k --definition verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module MODP-SPEC -w none
+```
+
+It exited 0 and printed `#Top`. The Haskell backend emitted
+`DecidePredicateUnknown` warnings while exploring/evaluating conditions, but
+ultimately closed the claim; no warning was substituted for the success
+criterion. Full bounded log:
+[positive proof](/audit-output/evidence/03-kprove-positive.log).
+
+The candidate's five concrete assertions also ran on the fresh LLVM definition
+with exit 0:
+[candidate concrete run](/audit-output/evidence/03-krun-candidate-tests.log).
+Reviewer-authored K assertions additionally cover `(0,1)`, `(0,101)`,
+`(1,1)`, `(3,5)`, and `(1101,101)` and pass with exit 0:
+[witness source](/audit-output/evidence/concrete-witnesses.py),
+[translated witness term](/audit-output/evidence/concrete-witnesses.mpy), and
+[witness K run](/audit-output/evidence/04-concrete-witness-krun.log).
+
+Dynamic reconstruction gate: **PASS** for the candidate's stated claim.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Plain-language claim
+
+Precondition: `N` and `P` are K integers with `N >= 0` and `P > 0`. The
+initial configuration is the empty module scope whose parent is the supplied
+builtins scope, with empty heap and stack, no return/exception, allocation
+counters at their initial values, and exit code zero.
+
+Execution: load `modpProgram`, then call its `modp` binding with `N` and `P`.
+
+Postcondition: execution reaches `specModp(N,P) ~> .K`, where
+`specModp(N,P) = pyMod(2 ^Int N, P)`. The module scope retains the exact
+`modp` closure; heap, stack, allocation counters, return state, exception, and
+exit code are the stated clean values.
+
+### Pinning evidence
+
+Trusted regeneration plus mechanical constructor-token expansion proves that
+the term named by `modpProgram` is the regenerated `solution.mpy` module:
+49 expanded constructor tokens equal all 49 regenerated tokens. Evidence:
+[pinning script](/audit-output/evidence/pinning_compare.py) and
+[token comparison](/audit-output/evidence/04-pinning-token-compare.log).
+
+An auxiliary K configuration claim also closes with `#Top` after frontend
+function expansion:
+[pinning claim](/audit-output/evidence/pinning.k) and
+[pinning proof](/audit-output/evidence/04-pinning-kprove.log).
+This is an immutable-artifact connection; the aliases are manually maintained,
+so lack of automatic source-to-alias regeneration remains a maintenance
+observation, not a current identity gap.
+
+There are no helper or loop claims. The entry claim executes the actual
+translated closure body through the supplied module load, call, binding,
+strict evaluation, return, and pop rules.
+
+Body sensitivity was tested by changing the executed program term itself from
+base 2 to base 3 while keeping the original base-2 obligation. The mutated
+definition built successfully. On satisfying ground input `(1,5)`, `kprove`
+exited 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState` and the concrete residual `3 ~> .K`,
+where the original body/result is 2:
+[body mutant](/audit-output/evidence/verification-body-mutant.k),
+[ground mutant claim](/audit-output/evidence/spec-body-mutant-ground.k),
+[mutant build](/audit-output/evidence/04-body-mutant-kompile.log), and
+[mutant rejection](/audit-output/evidence/04-body-mutant-ground-kprove.log).
+
+Ground postcondition substitutions are recorded in
+[ground witnesses](/audit-output/evidence/04-ground-witnesses.log). All five
+generated results equal `pyMod(2 ^Int N,P)`/`pow(2,n,p)`. The canonical agrees
+on four and has the already-described `(0,1)` disagreement.
+
+Real-program pinning and result constraint: **PASS**.
+
+Intent/domain adequacy: **FAIL**. The formal precondition materially narrows
+the unstated-precondition HumanEval integer domain to `n >= 0, p > 0`. The
+benchmark prompt explicitly maps this kind of `SOUND-BUT-LIMITED` finding to
+`FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+The reviewer inventoried all 26 applicable K source files (24 supplied files,
+`verification.k`, and `spec.k`):
+
+| Item | Count |
+|---|---:|
+| Total records | 935 |
+| Syntax declarations | 230 |
+| Rules | 698 |
+| Contexts | 5 |
+| Configurations | 1 |
+| Claims | 1 |
+| Equational rules | 453 |
+| Operational rules | 245 |
+| Function declarations | 149 |
+| `total` declarations | 107 |
+| `no-evaluators` opaque declarations | 22 |
+| Priority-bearing records | 52 |
+| `owise` records | 29 |
+| `concrete` records | 54 |
+
+No local `[simplification]` or `[functional]` record was found. The complete
+source-located statements and attributes are in
+[rule inventory](/audit-output/evidence/05-rule-inventory.log), produced by
+[rule_inventory.py](/audit-output/evidence/rule_inventory.py).
+Every record has an explicit proof-path, declaration, supplied-unused,
+domain-limited-unused, or opaque-unused disposition in
+[rule assessment](/audit-output/evidence/05-rule-assessment.log), produced by
+[rule_assessment.py](/audit-output/evidence/rule_assessment.py).
+
+The 935 dispositions are:
+
+- 70 accepted proof-path records;
+- 181 accepted unused declarations;
+- 643 accepted supplied-unused rules;
+- 19 domain-limited but unused rules; and
+- 22 supplied opaque trust boundaries, all unused here.
+
+### Submitted-program construct map
+
+The material path is:
+
+| Submitted construct | Declaration and semantic rules |
+|---|---|
+| `Module`, statement sequence | `syntax.k:56,61`; `core.k:124-127` |
+| `FuncDef("modp",...)` | `syntax.k:53`; `functions.k:14-16` |
+| docstring `Expr(Str(...))` | `syntax.k:13,52`; `str.k:13-17`; `controls.k:48` |
+| call and two arguments | `syntax.k:28`; `call.k:20-21,69-75`; `core.k:185-191,194` |
+| names `modp`, `n`, `p` | `syntax.k:12`; `core.k:130-154` |
+| return and frame pop | `syntax.k:50`; `functions.k:78-90` |
+| `2 ** n` | `syntax.k:15` sequential strictness; `operators.k:12`; `int.k:17` |
+| exponent result `% p` | same sequential dispatch; `int.k:15,19-20` |
+| exact program aliases | `verification.k:9-17` |
+| result summary | `verification.k:22-24` |
+
+Evaluation order is left-to-right: the inner exponentiation evaluates literal
+2 and `n`, then the outer modulo evaluates that result and `p`. Name binding is
+pinned by the exact module and callee scopes. The closure call creates one
+frame, binds both arguments, and the return rule pops that existing frame.
+There is no heap allocation or state mutation on this body. The only persistent
+state change is installation of the module-level `modp` closure, which the
+postcondition explicitly records.
+
+The relevant guards are complete on the formal precondition:
+
+- integer exponentiation requires a nonnegative exponent, supplied by `N >= 0`;
+- `pyMod` uses integer remainder and is defined on this path because `P > 0`;
+- lookup deterministically finds the locally installed closure and then bound
+  parameters; and
+- the call continuation and stack shape exactly match the return/pop rules.
+
+### Proof-local extension classification
+
+`modpBody` and `modpProgram` are definitional aliases. Their unconditional,
+non-overlapping equations name the exact regenerated constructors. They do not
+replace an invocation or skip semantics.
+
+`specModp` is a guarded definitional summary used only in the destination. It
+reduces to `pyMod(2 ^Int N,P)`. It is not present in operational execution and
+is not an oracle shared by a bridge and the postcondition.
+
+There are no proof-local priority rules, operational bridges, opaque symbols,
+totality assumptions, lemmas, or simplifications. Consequently, no
+proof-specific rule encodes the task answer, fabricates a result, or preempts a
+material source operation.
+
+### Supplied semantics limitations
+
+The supplied language is intentionally a minimal Python subset. The exhaustive
+review records 22 opaque symbols (float operations, sort summaries, and MD5);
+none occurs in the submitted term, path conditions, or postcondition, so no

# Independent adversarial review: 49-modp

This audit reconstructed the candidate from source under the supplied semantics.
The positive K claim is sound and non-vacuous on its stated domain, but it
materially narrows the HumanEval source-contract domain without a source
precondition authorizing that restriction. Under the benchmark-specific
decision rule, that is not a legitimate proof of the full task.

## 1. Input and provenance integrity

`/audit-input.json` declares:

- problem `49-modp`, condition `semantics`;
- `record_layout = legacy-selected-stage1`;
- `semantics_mode = SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`; and
- complete input provenance with the launcher paths supplied through
  `container_paths`.

The launcher and provenance gate passed:

- `/audit-campaign-lock.json` is JSON-equal to the `audit_campaign` block and
  has the recorded SHA-256
  `ad5dfcc006af70c4d0d2c6641f0878a6c54a266e9ad2b54cd225b2381a78d745`.
- The required layout records are readable regular files:
  `/run.json`, `/task.json`, `/generation-result.json`,
  `/generation-evidence/invocation.json`, `metrics.json`,
  `codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`, `prompt.txt`, and the structured trace.
  `usage.json` is present and was inspected. Historical
  `runtime-metrics.json` is absent, which is permitted for this layout.
- The full generation output (14,319 lines) and all 181 JSONL trace records
  were read. The trace contains 38 tool inputs, 13 `kprove` command mentions,
  seven `kompile` command mentions, and no patch targeting
  `reference-semantics/`.
- Every launcher-recorded scalar file hash checked by the reviewer matches.
- Candidate `prompt.py` and `py2mpy.py` are byte-identical to the trusted
  mounts.
- The candidate and trusted supplied-semantics trees have exactly the same 24
  files, path types, and bytes. Neither tree contains a symlink. The required
  trusted semantics mount is present, consistent with `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`.
- All five required proof artifacts are nonempty regular files. Candidate
  caches were not copied or reused.

Evidence:
[integrity log](/audit-output/evidence/01-integrity.log),
[record scan](/audit-output/evidence/01-generation-record-scan.log), and
[trace action extraction](/audit-output/evidence/01-generation-trace-actions.log).
The reviewer scripts are
[integrity_check.py](/audit-output/evidence/integrity_check.py) and
[generation_record_scan.py](/audit-output/evidence/generation_record_scan.py).

There is no audit-infrastructure breach.

## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks

### Source contract and implementations

The trusted prompt declares `modp(n: int, p: int)` and says: “Return 2^n
modulo p (be aware of numerics).” It gives five positive-modulus,
nonnegative-exponent examples, but states no input precondition.

The trusted canonical implementation initializes `ret = 1`, loops over
`range(n)`, updates `ret = (2 * ret) % p`, and returns `ret`.

The submitted program is:

```python
def modp(n: int, p: int):
    """Return 2^n modulo p."""
    return (2 ** n) % p
```

Running the trusted translator in scratch regenerated `solution.mpy` with byte
identity (exit 0):
[regeneration log](/audit-output/evidence/02-regeneration.log) and
[regenerated term](/audit-output/evidence/regenerated-solution.mpy).

### Independent differential test

The reviewer-authored
[differential_test.py](/audit-output/evidence/differential_test.py) imports the
trusted canonical and generated entries under distinct module names. It
exercised:

- all five documented examples;
- `n = 0` (the canonical loop's empty boundary), `n = 1`, and nearby values;
- `p = 1`, `p = 2`, and nearby values;
- exponent boundaries 63/64/65, a large `(4096, 65537)` case;
- a complete grid `0 <= n <= 32`, `1 <= p <= 64`; and
- 500 deterministic generated pairs with `0 <= n <= 5000`,
  `1 <= p <= 10000`.

There were 2,619 unique cases. The generated program agreed with the prompt's
`pow(2, n, p)` value on all of them. It differed from the canonical once:

```text
n=0, p=1: canonical=1, generated=0, pow(2,0,1)=0
```

Thus the generated program is mathematically faithful to the prose at that
boundary, while the canonical loop has an empty-loop boundary defect. The
command intentionally exits 1 so this disagreement cannot be overlooked:
[differential log](/audit-output/evidence/02-differential.log).

The more serious adequacy issue is domain scope. The prompt's annotated source
domain is two integers and contains no `n >= 0` or `p > 0` precondition. Even
if modulus zero is excluded as undefined, the canonical terminates on negative
`n` and on negative nonzero `p`. Diagnostics show material differences:

```text

(0, -5): canonical 1, generated -4
```

The candidate theorem excludes all such inputs. The examples do not create a
source-level restriction, and finitely observed test ranges cannot do so.

Only source artifacts were copied to `/tmp/audit-work/49-modp`; the trusted
reference-semantics tree was used, and no candidate-built definition or cache
was reused. Tool versions were independently checked as K v7.1.293:
[toolchain log](/audit-output/evidence/03-toolchain.log).

```text

  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
  --output-definition runtime-kompiled -w none
```

[LLVM build log](/audit-output/evidence/03-kompile-llvm.log).

```text

  --main-module MODP-VERIFICATION --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
```

[Haskell build log](/audit-output/evidence/03-kompile-haskell.log).

The candidate has exactly one positive target claim. Its independent command
was:

```text
kprove spec.k --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module MODP-SPEC -w none
```

It exited 0 and printed `#Top`. The Haskell backend emitted
`DecidePredicateUnknown` warnings while exploring/evaluating conditions, but
ultimately closed the claim; no warning was substituted for the success
criterion. Full bounded log:
[positive proof](/audit-output/evidence/03-kprove-positive.log).

[witness K run](/audit-output/evidence/04-concrete-witness-krun.log).
